- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 30-day horizon.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) after a spike, model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at 1–2% below recent peak.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >+5% from 18-day mean), model frequently overreacts; apply downward bias of 2–5% for next 7–14 days.
- When sentiment is neutral (0.00–0.33) and history shows low volatility, model tends to underestimate; add 1–2% to forecast for next 10–20 days.
- If model forecast is >+10% above 18-day moving average, reduce by 1–3% for next 5–10 days unless sentiment is strongly bullish.
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 18-day mean), model often fails to recognize; adjust forecast downward by 1–3% for next 7–14 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is mixed or volatile, model tends to overfit recent spikes; use 18-day moving average as baseline and adjust ±1–2% based on sentiment direction.
